Singapore: Partly passes, unchanged from baseline. Checked against CONCEPT-01 (docs/concepts/singapore-on-foot.png). The landmarks and architecture read clearly as Singapore: pastel shophouse five-foot way with pilasters and timber shutters, the Tembusu Food Centre hawker hall with its red steel roof and Kaya Toast / Soup Noodles / Tea & Coffee stalls, MBS-like triple towers, Supertree-like grove, HDB blocks with void decks, a Kampong Sirih Road street sign, double-yellow kerb lines and left-hand traffic. The street life fails the concept. CONCEPT-01 shows a dense, diverse crowd on the five-foot way, Peranakan floor tiles, bollards, drains and potted plants, and bilingual, characterful signage. Ours has plain grey or brick slabs, generic black sans-serif boards ('Rice Shop', 'Clinic', 'Sari Textiles'), and only a handful of pedestrians. The pedestrians near the player are clones of one young male model in recoloured shirts, and he appears to share the player's head and hair. There are no aunties, uncles, schoolchildren or office workers, and no ethnic or age variety. The city reads as Singapore from its skyline and buildings, not from its people.. Judge: A wins all four pairs clearly, and none were close enough to call INDISTINGUISHABLE. Pair 2 was the nearest. The four B frames look like one build (same character, same Singapore-style city) and fail in the same ways every time. Large, perfectly repeating paver floors fill 40-60% of the frame with no wear or props. Set dressing is thin, with identical shrubs at even spacing. The character looks plastic, with a solid lump of hair and stiff idle or walk poses. Signage and the HUD look like placeholders: floating street labels, a 'Clinic' sign, a flat grid minimap. The distant towers are plain boxes, the sky is a flat gradient, and daylight landmarks glow neon. In pairs 1 and 3, the warm key on the character doesn't light the background buildings. B's real strengths are its golden-hour warmth, some dappled shadows (pair 2), decent tree shapes, recognisable landmarks and a few pedestrians, so the lighting direction is promising but the frames don't yet read as a premium game. Only pair 4 A truly wows. Pairs 1 and 3 A are very good premium frames, and pair 2 A looks dated but is better composed than B. Highest-value fixes for B, in order: (1) dress and break up the ground and the area near the character, (2) improve the character's materials and poses, (3) add a sky with clouds, haze with distance and a sun that lights the whole frame. Blinding note: A in pairs 2 and 3 has a corner logo, so the blind test was imperfect there. I judged only on what the frames show, and the verdicts would be the same without the logo.
